title: Repair refutation proposal
observation: Current isolated fixture contract: POST /preview accepts JSON field url and intentionally fetches public URLs. Public callbacks are allowed. Private destinations are prohibited. Future tests may use only owned, authorized fixture public/private canaries. A private-probe success and the corresponding blocked private-probe outcome must address the same destination-policy consequence; public/invalid-URL controls alone do not refute private access. Evidence must differentiate server-side private retrieval from ordinary callbacks and transport errors. No target test has run; do not execute probes in this correction task.
objective: Future destination-policy test has permitted public baseline, positive private access evidence and a matching negative private-probe outcome; no execution is required now. Use only retained current-operation fixture evidence; do not execute future tests.
criterion: Future destination-policy test has permitted public baseline, positive private access evidence and a matching negative private-probe outcome; no execution is required now.

preconditions: Authorized isolated fixture with private canary reachable only from server network
Policy documentation confirms public URLs permitted and private network destinations prohibited
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: Server-side request forgery allowing retrieval from prohibited private network destinations via user-controlled URL in POST /preview
hypotheses.attacker_controlled_input: URL parameter supplied in POST /preview request body
safe_test_steps: Send POST /preview with URL pointing to owned public canary and record response
Send POST /preview with URL pointing to owned private canary in prohibited private range and record response
Compare private probe response to public canary control and to a no-op control
positive_expectations: Server returns content from private canary indicating server-side fetch succeeded from a prohibited private destination
Response contains private canary data not reachable from the client and differs from the public canary response
negative_expectations: Public canary request returns expected public content with no private data
Control request with no URL or invalid URL returns error without private retrieval
required_evidence: Saved response bodies for public canary probe and private canary probe
Evidence that private canary is only reachable from server network and that response originates from server-side fetch

title: Review network future test
observation: Authorized isolated TCP gateway fixture: the caller controls destination_host and destination_port in CONNECT requests. Public owned destinations are permitted; a private owned listener is forbidden by connection policy. Listener logs and gateway records distinguish gateway-originated connections from client connections and transport failures. No connections have been executed.
objective: Review the retained future test against its evidence and frozen acceptance; do not execute probes.
criterion: The future test specifies supporting and matching refuting observations for each claimed policy violation; unrelated controls alone are insufficient.

hypotheses.observed_basis: Authorized isolated TCP gateway fixture: the caller controls destination_host and destination_port in CONNECT requests. Public owned destinations are permitted; a private owned listener is forbidden by connection policy. Listener logs and gateway records distinguish gateway-originated connections from client connections and transport failures. No connections have been executed.
preconditions: Authorized isolated fixture with owned canaries; establish enforcement and policy before future probes
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: Gateway connection-policy bypass to a prohibited private owned listener
hypotheses.attacker_controlled_input: destination_host and destination_port in the gateway CONNECT request
safe_test_steps: Establish policy and ownership of the public and private fixture listeners
Compare a permitted public-listener CONNECT control with a private-listener CONNECT probe
Save gateway decisions and listener logs to determine whether the private probe established a session
positive_expectations: The private probe establishes a gateway-originated session to the forbidden owned listener
negative_expectations: The public control connects successfully to the permitted listener
A syntactically invalid CONNECT request is rejected
required_evidence: Gateway decision records for both requests
Owned listener logs identifying connection origin

title: Review filesystem future test
observation: Authorized isolated source/filesystem fixture: read_document(relative_path) accepts a caller path and promises access only inside a configured document root. A controlled file outside that root is forbidden and has a unique marker. Source establishes a path join but leaves canonicalization enforcement unresolved. Fixture file ownership and audit records distinguish outside-root reads from permitted document reads. No file probes have been executed.
objective: Review the retained future test against its evidence and frozen acceptance; do not execute probes.
criterion: The future test specifies supporting and matching refuting observations for each claimed policy violation; unrelated controls alone are insufficient.

hypotheses.observed_basis: Authorized isolated source/filesystem fixture: read_document(relative_path) accepts a caller path and promises access only inside a configured document root. A controlled file outside that root is forbidden and has a unique marker. Source establishes a path join but leaves canonicalization enforcement unresolved. Fixture file ownership and audit records distinguish outside-root reads from permitted document reads. No file probes have been executed.
preconditions: Authorized isolated fixture with owned canaries; establish enforcement and policy before future probes
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: Path containment bypass reading a forbidden owned file outside the document root
safe_test_steps: Establish the allowed document root and forbidden outside-root owned canary with distinct contents
Read a permitted in-root control and submit a traversal path targeting the owned outside-root canary
Save returned content and file access audit records for the same caller
positive_expectations: The traversal probe returns the outside-root canary marker and audit records show its forbidden read
negative_expectations: The in-root control returns the permitted document
An invalid path type is rejected
required_evidence: Returned contents and file access audit records for both calls
